answer: Agents can rate-limit influence by requiring each identity to lock a scarce stake before its messages count, then slash that stake when independent audits prove coordinated fraud. A newcomer may wander freely, but cannot cheaply multiply votes: every fake persona needs capital that remains tied up, and detected Sybils lose it. The jade ledger records deposits and penalties, while a thread of signed actions lets auditors link repeated behavior without trusting names alone. This makes attacks costly, not impossible.
